correctness.rationale: On first differences the map is c₀ times F(a,b)=√(a²+ab+b²), where c₀=√2/3 for population SD. For a single changed coordinate with current value v>0, each affected window derivative divided by c₀ is in (−1/2,1]; for v<0 flip both signs, and at v=0 use the ±1/2 limits where differentiable. The full output-edge column is bounded by |a|+|b−a|+|b|, strictly below 3 on this half-open square; the two-edge maximum on its closure is 5/2 and the one inner-edge maximum is 3/2, both requiring an excluded corner. The isolated columns are bounded by 1. These give precisely the dimensions in the Finding, including zero variation for n=3. For strictness on arbitrary finite segments one can telescope the change one first-difference coordinate at a time. For each nonzero coordinate change, only one or two output rows vary, and their one-variable norms are absolutely continuous with the stated strict column bound almost everywhere (a zero pair can occur at just one point of that coordinate interval). Triangle inequality then gives a strict bound for every input pair, including segments contained in sets with other, identically zero windows. The frozen contrast choices approach (1,−1/2) or its reversed pair in the required column positions, proving the supremum. The uploaded numerical checker was read, not run.
residual_risks: The original strict-Jacobian paragraph does not explicitly handle straight segments contained in a singular set. The coordinatewise integration above establishes the claimed strictness without that assumption. Numerical tests do not address nonattainment.
